FISH — chord prototypes session axes chord ↗

1 · Classic chord — arrow ribbons

arcs = ns¹ components · ribbon = directed quotient edge, arrow at target · width = additive weight · black = trigger, orange = sampled

2 · Classic chord — one ribbon per direction

same data; each direction of a pair is its own ribbon anchored at its source arc (no arrows)

3 · Hierarchical edge bundling — ROS axis

leaves = data-phase F callbacks · nesting = ns¹ › ns² › node (cluster layout) · edges = F-level msg (grey→black) and state/polled (orange) · slider = bundling strength β (the "slider" of the axis, visually)
β 0.85

4 · Tri-sector — the three axes as 120° sectors

arcs: ROS classes (top, sized by CPU execution time) · OS executors (left: EX vertices — process-primary executors, type/threads; CPU execution time) · GPU streams (right, kernel time). Ribbons are NOT messages: each ribbon is the SAME set of facts seen from two axes (a meet cell) — e.g. "this namespace's callbacks ran in this process", "this namespace's callbacks submitted this much kernel time to this stream". width = total time (additive) · opacity = fact count (message size is not traced at the ROS layer — alpha uses counts; GPU ribbons show memcpy bytes in the tooltip).
